      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: If a PCR step was performed that specifically targets the IG/TR loci,
      the target and primer locations need to be provided here. This field holds an
      array of PCRTarget objects, so that multiplex PCR setups amplifying multiple
      loci at the same time can be annotated using one record per locus. PCR setups
      not targeting any specific locus must not annotate this field but select the
      appropriate library_generation_method instead.
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: NucleicAcidProcessing
    domain_of:
    - NucleicAcidProcessing
    - SampleProcessing
    range: PCRTarget
    multivalued: true
  complete_sequences:
    name: complete_sequences
    annotations:
      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: To be considered `complete`, the procedure used for library construction
      MUST generate sequences that 1) include the first V gene codon that encodes
      the mature polypeptide chain (i.e. after the leader sequence) and 2) include
      the last complete codon of the J gene (i.e. 1 bp 5' of the J->C splice site)
      and 3) provide sequence information for all positions between 1) and 2). To
      be considered `complete & untemplated`, the sections of the sequences defined
      in points 1) to 3) of the previous sentence MUST be untemplated, i.e. MUST NOT
      overlap with the primers used in library preparation. `mixed` should only be
      used if the procedure used for library construction will likely produce multiple
      categories of sequences in the given experiment. It SHOULD NOT be used as a
      replacement of a NULL value.
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: NucleicAcidProcessing
    domain_of:

    - SampleProcessing
    range: CompleteSequencesEnum
  physical_linkage:
    name: physical_linkage
    annotations:
      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: In case an experimental setup is used that physically links nucleic
      acids derived from distinct `Rearrangements` before library preparation, this
      field describes the mode of that linkage. All `hetero_*` terms indicate that
      in case of paired-read sequencing, the two reads should be expected to map to
      distinct IG/TR loci. `*_head-head` refers to techniques that link the 5' ends
      of transcripts in a single-cell context. `*_tail-head` refers to techniques
      that link the 3' end of one transcript to the 5' end of another one in a single-cell
      context. This term does not provide any information whether a continuous reading-frame
      between the two is generated. `*_prelinked` refers to constructs in which the
      linkage was already present on the DNA level (e.g. scFv).
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: NucleicAcidProcessing
    domain_of:
    - NucleicAcidProcessing
    - SampleProcessing
    range: PhysicalLinkageEnum

    - SampleProcessing

      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: If a PCR step was performed that specifically targets the IG/TR loci,
      the target and primer locations need to be provided here. This field holds an
      array of PCRTarget objects, so that multiplex PCR setups amplifying multiple
      loci at the same time can be annotated using one record per locus. PCR setups
      not targeting any specific locus must not annotate this field but select the
      appropriate library_generation_method instead.
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: SampleProcessing
    domain_of:
    - NucleicAcidProcessing
    - SampleProcessing
    range: PCRTarget
    multivalued: true
  complete_sequences:
    name: complete_sequences
    annotations:
      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: To be considered `complete`, the procedure used for library construction
      MUST generate sequences that 1) include the first V gene codon that encodes
      the mature polypeptide chain (i.e. after the leader sequence) and 2) include
      the last complete codon of the J gene (i.e. 1 bp 5' of the J->C splice site)
      and 3) provide sequence information for all positions between 1) and 2). To
      be considered `complete & untemplated`, the sections of the sequences defined
      in points 1) to 3) of the previous sentence MUST be untemplated, i.e. MUST NOT
      overlap with the primers used in library preparation. `mixed` should only be
      used if the procedure used for library construction will likely produce multiple
      categories of sequences in the given experiment. It SHOULD NOT be used as a
      replacement of a NULL value.
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: SampleProcessing
    domain_of:
    - NucleicAcidProcessing
    - SampleProcessing
    range: CompleteSequencesEnum
  physical_linkage:
    name: physical_linkage
    annotations:
      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: false
    description: In case an experimental setup is used that physically links nucleic
      acids derived from distinct `Rearrangements` before library preparation, this
      field describes the mode of that linkage. All `hetero_*` terms indicate that
      in case of paired-read sequencing, the two reads should be expected to map to
      distinct IG/TR loci. `*_head-head` refers to techniques that link the 5' ends
      of transcripts in a single-cell context. `*_tail-head` refers to techniques
      that link the 3' end of one transcript to the 5' end of another one in a single-cell
      context. This term does not provide any information whether a continuous reading-frame
      between the two is generated. `*_prelinked` refers to constructs in which the
      linkage was already present on the DNA level (e.g. scFv).
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: SampleProcessing
    domain_of:
    - NucleicAcidProcessing
    - SampleProcessing
    range: PhysicalLinkageEnum

    annotations:
      nullable:
        tag: nullable
        value: true
    description: ID of sequencing run assigned by the sequencing facility
    from_schema: https://github.com/vdjserver/vdjserver-airr-schema
    rank: 1000
    owner: SampleProcessing
    domain_of:
    - SequencingRun
    - SampleProcessing
    range: string
  total_reads_passing_qc_filter:

    annotations:

docs.title: Slot: activity
docs.text: Default slot description

docs.title: Slot: adc
docs.text: List of production repositories. Each entry is keyed by the repository id.

docs.title: Slot: adc_publish_date
docs.text: Date the study was first published in the AIRR Data Commons.

docs.title: Slot: adc_update_date
docs.text: Date the study data was updated in the AIRR Data Commons.

docs.title: Slot: affiliation
docs.text: ROR of the contributor's primary affiliation. Note that ROR are only minted for institutions, not from individuals institutes, divisions or departments.

docs.title: Slot: affiliation_department
docs.text: Additional information regarding the contributor's primary affiliation. Can be used to specify individual institutes, divisions or departments.

docs.title: Slot: age
docs.text: Age of subject expressed as a time interval. If singular time point then min == max in the time interval.

docs.title: Slot: age_event
docs.text: Event in the study schedule to which Age refers. For NCBI BioSample this MUST be sampling. For other implementations submitters need to be aware that there is currently no mechanism to encode to potential delta between Age event and Sample collection time, hence the chosen events should be in temporal proximity.

docs.title: Slot: agent
docs.text: Default slot description

docs.title: Slot: aliases
docs.text: Alternative names for this sequence

docs.title: Slot: aligned_sequence
docs.text: Aligned sequence if this delineation provides an alignment. An aligned sequence should always be provided for IMGT delineations.

docs.title: Slot: alignment_labels
docs.text: One string for each codon in the aligned_sequence indicating the label of that codon according to the numbering of the delineation scheme if it provides one.

docs.title: Slot: allele_description_id
docs.text: Unique identifier of this AlleleDescription within the file. Typically, generated by the repository hosting the record.

docs.title: Slot: allele_description_ref
docs.text: Unique reference to the allele description, in standardized form (Repo:Label:Version)

docs.title: Slot: allele_descriptions
docs.text: list of allele_descriptions in the germline set

docs.title: Slot: allele_name
docs.text: Allele name as allocated by the inference pipeline

docs.title: Slot: allele_similarity_cluster_designation
docs.text: ID of the similarity cluster used in this germline set, if designated

docs.title: Slot: allele_similarity_cluster_member_id
docs.text: Membership ID of the allele within the similarity cluster, if a cluster is designated

docs.title: Slot: allowedUses
docs.text: file path

docs.title: Slot: analysis_provenance_id
docs.text: Identifier for machine-readable PROV model of analysis provenance

docs.title: Slot: analysis_uuid
docs.text: Default slot description

docs.title: Slot: anatomic_site
docs.text: The anatomic location of the tissue, e.g. Inguinal, femur

docs.title: Slot: ancestry_population
docs.text: Broad geographic origin of ancestry (continent)

docs.title: Slot: antigen
docs.text: The substance against which the receptor was tested. This can be any substance that stimulates an adaptive immune response in the host, either through antibody production or by T cell activation after presentation via an MHC molecule.

docs.title: Slot: antigen_source_species
docs.text: The species from which the antigen was isolated

docs.title: Slot: antigen_type
docs.text: The type of antigen before processing by the immune system.

docs.title: Slot: associationIds
docs.text: object associations

docs.title: Slot: async_base_url
docs.text: Base ADC ASYNC API URL for repository

docs.title: Slot: async_host
docs.text: Hostname for repository

docs.title: Slot: base_url
docs.text: Base ADC URL for repository

docs.title: Slot: biomaterial_provider
docs.text: Name and address of the entity providing the sample

docs.title: Slot: c_alignment_end
docs.text: End position of the C gene alignment in both the sequence_alignment and germline_alignment fields (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_alignment_start
docs.text: Start position of the C gene alignment in both the sequence_alignment and germline_alignment fields (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_call
docs.text: Constant region gene with allele. If referring to a known reference sequence in a database the relevant gene/allele nomenclature should be followed (e.g., IGHG1*01 if using IMGT/GENE-DB).

docs.title: Slot: c_cigar
docs.text: CIGAR string for the C gene alignment.

docs.title: Slot: c_germline_alignment
docs.text: Aligned constant region germline sequence spanning the same region as the c_sequence_alignment field and including the same set of corrections and spacers (if any).

docs.title: Slot: c_germline_alignment_aa
docs.text: Amino acid translation of the c_germline_aligment field.

docs.title: Slot: c_germline_end
docs.text: Alignment end position in the C gene reference sequence (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_germline_start
docs.text: Alignment start position in the C gene reference sequence (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_identity
docs.text: Fractional identity for the C gene alignment.

docs.title: Slot: c_score
docs.text: Alignment score for the C gene alignment.

docs.title: Slot: c_sequence_alignment
docs.text: Aligned portion of query sequence assigned to the constant region, including any indel corrections or numbering spacers.

docs.title: Slot: c_sequence_alignment_aa
docs.text: Amino acid translation of the c_sequence_alignment field.

docs.title: Slot: c_sequence_end
docs.text: End position of the C gene in the query sequence (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_sequence_start
docs.text: Start position of the C gene in the query sequence (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: c_support
docs.text: C gene alignment E-value, p-value, likelihood, probability or other similar measure of support for the C gene assignment as defined by the alignment tool.

docs.title: Slot: cdr1
docs.text: Nucleotide sequence of the aligned CDR1 region.

docs.title: Slot: cdr1_aa
docs.text: Amino acid translation of the cdr1 field.

docs.title: Slot: cdr2
docs.text: Nucleotide sequence of the aligned CDR2 region.

docs.title: Slot: cdr2_aa
docs.text: Amino acid translation of the cdr2 field.

docs.title: Slot: cdr3
docs.text: Nucleotide sequence of the aligned CDR3 region.

docs.title: Slot: cdr3_aa
docs.text: Amino acid translation of the cdr3 field.

docs.title: Slot: cdr3_end
docs.text: CDR3 end position in the query sequence (1-based closed interval).

docs.title: Slot: cell_isolation
docs.text: Description of the procedure used for marker-based isolation or enrich cells

docs.title: Slot: cell_label
docs.text: Free text cell type annotation. Primarily used for annotating cell types that are not provided in the Cell Ontology.

docs.title: Slot: cell_number
docs.text: Total number of cells that went into the experiment

docs.title: Slot: cell_phenotype
docs.text: List of cellular markers and their expression levels used to isolate the cell population.

docs.title: Slot: cell_processing_protocol
docs.text: Description of the methods applied to the sample including cell preparation/ isolation/enrichment and nucleic acid extraction. This should closely mirror the Materials and methods section in the manuscript.

docs.title: Slot: cell_quality
docs.text: Relative amount of viable cells after preparation and (if applicable) thawing

docs.title: Slot: cell_species
docs.text: Binomial designation of the species from which the analyzed cells originate. Typically, this value should be identical to species, in which case it SHOULD NOT be set explicitly. However, there are valid experimental setups in which the two might differ, e.g., chimeric animal models. If set, this key will overwrite the species information for all lower layers of the schema.

docs.title: Slot: cell_storage
docs.text: TRUE if cells were cryo-preserved between isolation and further processing

docs.title: Slot: cell_type
docs.text: Cell type (source). Most often the type should be "observed," meaning it corresponds to an actual physical sample that was sequenced. Other allowed values are "simulated," i.e. the Cells were generated in silico and there is no linked Subject/Sample metadata, and "inferred" for Cells that are phylogenetically reconstructed from observed sequences. Inferred Cells should be assigned to a Repertoire with repertoire_type=inferred.

docs.title: Slot: cells_per_reaction
docs.text: Number of cells for each biological replicate

docs.title: Slot: chromosome
docs.text: chromosome on which the gene is located

docs.title: Slot: city
docs.text: Default slot description

docs.title: Slot: clone_class

docs.title: Slot: clone_count
docs.text: Absolute count of the size (number of members) of this clone in the repertoire. This could simply be the number of sequences (Rearrangement records) observed in this clone, the number of distinct cell barcodes (unique cell_id values), or a more sophisticated calculation appropriate to the experimental protocol. Absolute count is provided versus a frequency so that downstream analysis tools can perform their own normalization.

docs.title: Slot: complete_sequences
docs.text: To be considered complete, the procedure used for library construction MUST generate sequences that 1) include the first V gene codon that encodes the mature polypeptide chain (i.e. after the leader sequence) and 2) include the last complete codon of the J gene (i.e. 1 bp 5' of the J->C splice site) and 3) provide sequence information for all positions between 1) and 2). To be considered complete & untemplated, the sections of the sequences defined in points 1) to 3) of the previous sentence MUST be untemplated, i.e. MUST NOT overlap with the primers used in library preparation. mixed should only be used if the procedure used for library construction will likely produce multiple categories of sequences in the given experiment. It SHOULD NOT be used as a replacement of a NULL value.

docs.title: Slot: complete_vdj
docs.text: True if the sequence alignment spans the entire V(D)J region. Meaning, sequence_alignment includes both the first V gene codon that encodes the mature polypeptide chain (i.e., after the leader sequence) and the last complete codon of the J gene (i.e., before the J-C splice site). This does not require an absence of deletions within the internal FWR and CDR regions of the alignment.

docs.text: If a PCR step was performed that specifically targets the IG/TR loci, the target and primer locations need to be provided here. This field holds an array of PCRTarget objects, so that multiplex PCR setups amplifying multiple loci at the same time can be annotated using one record per locus. PCR setups not targeting any specific locus must not annotate this field but select the appropriate library_generation_method instead.

docs.title: Slot: pcr_target_locus
docs.text: Designation of the target locus. Note that this field uses a controlled vocubulary that is meant to provide a generic classification of the locus, not necessarily the correct designation according to a specific nomenclature.

docs.text: End position of the peptide within the reference protein sequence

docs.title: Slot: peptide_sequence_aa
docs.text: The actual peptide sequence against which the receptor reactivity was measured. This field should be used as a convenience for antigens of antigen_type protein or peptide.

docs.title: Slot: peptide_start

docs.title: Slot: permission

docs.title: Slot: phasing
docs.text: Chromosomal phasing indicator. Alleles with the same value are inferred to be located on the same chromosome.

docs.title: Slot: physical_linkage
docs.text: In case an experimental setup is used that physically links nucleic acids derived from distinct Rearrangements before library preparation, this field describes the mode of that linkage. All hetero_* terms indicate that in case of paired-read sequencing, the two reads should be expected to map to distinct IG/TR loci. *_head-head refers to techniques that link the 5' ends of transcripts in a single-cell context. *_tail-head refers to techniques that link the 3' end of one transcript to the 5' end of another one in a single-cell context. This term does not provide any information whether a continuous reading-frame between the two is generated. *_prelinked refers to constructs in which the linkage was already present on the DNA level (e.g. scFv).

docs.title: Slot: property_type
docs.text: Keyword describing the property type and detection method used to measure the property value. The following keywords are recommended, but custom property types are also valid: "mrna_expression_by_read_count", "protein_expression_by_fluorescence_intensity", "antigen_bait_binding_by_fluorescence_intensity", "protein_expression_by_dna_barcode_count" and "antigen_bait_binding_by_dna_barcode_count".

docs.title: Slot: quality
docs.text: The Sanger/Phred quality scores for assessment of sequence quality. Phred quality scores from 0 to 93 are encoded using ASCII 33 to 126 (Used by Illumina from v1.8.)

docs.title: Slot: qualityScoreMetadataUuid
docs.text: Default slot description

docs.title: Slot: quality_alignment
docs.text: Sanger/Phred quality scores for assessment of sequence_alignment quality. Phred quality scores from 0 to 93 are encoded using ASCII 33 to 126 (Used by Illumina from v1.8.)

docs.title: Slot: quality_thresholds
docs.text: How/if sequences were removed from (4) based on base quality scores

docs.title: Slot: raw_file

docs.title: Slot: reactivity_method
docs.text: The methodology used to assess/classify reactivity. This should be either the assay utlizied in the experiment, delineated as "annotated" if annotated from an external source (e.g. IEDB), or inferred if imputed using a computational method. In future versions we anticipate this field being an enumerated type, and it is strongly recommended that users utilize one of the following keywords in this field if appropriate: native_protein, MHC_peptide_multimer, annotated, inferred.

docs.title: Slot: reactivity_readout
docs.text: Reactivity measurement read-out. For physical assays, this should describe what was measured. For inferred and annotated methods this should indicate a confidence/quality level for the inference/annotation. In future versions we anticipate this field being an enumerated type, and it is strongly recommended that users utilize one of the following keywords in this field if appropriate: fluorescence_intensity, barcode_count, confidence.

docs.title: Slot: reactivity_ref
docs.text: Comma separated list of CURIE identifiers of external reactivity records (e.g. IEDB_EPITOPE:1616345, https://https://www.iedb.org/epitope/1616345) associated with this Rearrangement. Order and length of reactivity_id and reactivity_ref are independent.

docs.text: Rearrangement type (source). Most often the type should be "observed," meaning it corresponds to an actual physical sample that was sequenced. Other allowed values are "simulated," i.e. the Rearrangements were generated in silico and there is no linked Subject/Sample metadata, and "inferred" for Rearrangements that are phylogenetically reconstructed from observed sequences. Inferred Rearrangements should be assigned to a Repertoire with repertoire_type=inferred.

docs.title: Slot: receptor_ref

docs.title: Slot: receptor_type

docs.title: Slot: receptor_variable_domain_1_aa
docs.text: Complete amino acid sequence of the mature variable domain of the Ig heavy, TCR beta or TCR delta chain. The mature variable domain is defined as encompassing all AA from and including first AA after the the signal peptide to and including the last AA that is completely encoded by the J gene.

docs.title: Slot: receptor_variable_domain_1_locus

docs.title: Slot: receptor_variable_domain_2_aa
docs.text: Complete amino acid sequence of the mature variable domain of the Ig light, TCR alpha or TCR gamma chain. The mature variable domain is defined as encompassing all AA from and including first AA after the the signal peptide to and including the last AA that is completely encoded by the J gene.

docs.title: Slot: receptor_variable_domain_2_locus
